config.title: Auth Context

intro.title: Auth Context
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple authentication context to manage user login state across your Vue application. You'll learn how to use Vue's reactive system to create shared state that multiple components can access. The main technologies involved are Vue's reactive ref for state management and provide/inject for passing data through the component tree. By the end, you'll understand how to create a centralized auth store that tracks whether a user is logged in and make that information available to different parts of your app without prop drilling.
intro.usecase: Auth Context is a fundamental pattern for managing user authentication state across an entire Vue application, similar to how a dashboard or admin panel needs to know if a user is logged in to display personalized content or restrict access. For example, in an e-commerce site, the shopping cart icon, user profile menu, and checkout page all need immediate access to the current user's login status and details without prop-drilling through every component. This pattern is essential for building secure, maintainable applications where authentication state must be consistently available, such as in banking apps that show account balances only after login or SaaS platforms that conditionally render features based on user roles.

objectives: Construct a reactive authentication state using Vue's Composition API
Initialize and configure a centralized auth store with user data and tokens
Implement authentication methods for login, logout, and token validation
Bind auth state to components using provide/inject patterns
Control component rendering based on authentication status
Integrate auth context with protected routes and API calls
Manipulate auth state in response to user interactions
Update UI elements dynamically when auth state changes

steps.title: Import Vue and createApp
steps.instruction: Import Vue and createApp from 'vue' to initialize the Vue application.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and createApp from the 'vue' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing modules in JavaScript
import { createApp } from 'vue';
steps.seedCode: // Import Vue and createApp from 'vue' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue and createApp modules are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: Vue and createApp are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Vue and createApp, which are essential for setting up the Vue application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Vue and createApp from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import Vue and createApp from 'vue'.

steps.title: Create and export AuthContext using provide/inject
steps.instruction: Create a Symbol named 'AuthContext' and export it as a constant.
steps.hint: Use Symbol() to create a unique identifier for your context, then export it with 'export const'.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Vue and createApp from 'vue' here

// Create and export AuthContext symbol here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a unique AuthContext symbol ready to use with Vue's provide/inject API.
successCriteria: AuthContext is created as a Symbol and exported as a constant.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a unique AuthContext symbol that can be used throughout your app.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using Symbol() and exporting it with 'export const'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Create a Symbol named 'AuthContext' and export it as a constant.

steps.title: Create AuthProvider component with reactive state
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named AuthProvider that returns a template with a single root element (like a div). The component should accept a children prop and render it inside the root element.
steps.hint: In Vue, functional components can be created using either a function declaration or an arrow function. Remember to include a return statement with JSX or a template.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a basic AuthProvider component that can wrap child content.
successCriteria: AuthProvider component is defined as a function that accepts children and returns a template with a single root element containing the children.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the AuthProvider component structure. This will serve as the wrapper for your authentication context.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your AuthProvider component accepts children and returns a template with a single root element containing those children.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AuthProvider component isn't properly defined. It should be a function that returns JSX/template with children rendered inside a root element.

steps.title: Initialize reactive auth state in AuthProvider
steps.instruction: Inside your AuthProvider component, create a reactive object called 'authState' that contains 'user' (set to null) and 'isAuthenticated' (set to false).
steps.hint: Use Vue's reactive() function to make the object reactive. The object should have two properties with initial values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthProvider component will have a reactive 'authState' object ready to track authentication data.
successCriteria: A reactive object named 'authState' is created with 'user: null' and 'isAuthenticated: false' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the reactive authentication state object.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using reactive() and your object has both 'user' and 'isAuthenticated' properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Create a reactive object with the two required properties inside the AuthProvider's setup function.

steps.title: Create login handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthProvider component's setup function, create a function named login that updates the auth state's isAuthenticated to true and sets the user property to an object with a name property.
steps.hint: Define a function that modifies the reactive auth state you initialized earlier. Remember to use the state variable you created.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a login function inside the AuthProvider component that can update the authentication state.
successCriteria: The AuthProvider component contains a login function that sets isAuthenticated to true and assigns a user object with a name property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the login handler function that updates the auth state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it properly updates both isAuthenticated and user properties in the auth state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The login function is missing or doesn't correctly update the auth state. Review how to modify reactive state in Vue.

steps.title: Create logout handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthProvider component's setup function, create a logout handler function that clears the auth state by setting user to null and isAuthenticated to false.
steps.hint: Define a function named logout that updates the reactive auth state object.
steps.expectedOutcome: A logout function is added to the AuthProvider's setup that properly clears the authentication state.
successCriteria: The logout function is defined and correctly updates the auth state to clear user data and set isAuthenticated to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the logout handler function that clears the authentication state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a logout function, but make sure it properly updates both the user and isAuthenticated properties in the auth state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The logout function is missing or doesn't properly clear the authentication state. Check that you're updating both user and isAuthenticated properties.

steps.title: Provide auth state and handlers via provide()
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthProvider component's setup function, use Vue's provide() function to expose the auth state and handler functions via the AuthContext symbol.
steps.hint: Call provide() with two arguments: first the AuthContext symbol, then an object containing the reactive state and handler functions.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthProvider component will make the auth state and handlers available to all child components via the AuthContext.
successCriteria: The provide() function is called with AuthContext as the first argument and an object containing the auth state and handler functions as the second argument.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully used provide() to make the auth context available to child components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling provide() with both arguments: the AuthContext symbol and an object containing the auth state and handlers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The provide() function needs to be called inside the setup function with the correct arguments.

steps.title: Create main App component structure
steps.instruction: Create the main App component that will use the AuthProvider. The component should be a named constant and return a template with a root div.
steps.hint: Define a constant named App with a setup function that returns a template. The template should contain a root div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined with a setup function that returns a template containing a root div.
successCriteria: App component is created as a constant with a setup function that returns a template containing a root div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main App component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the App component has a setup function that returns a template with a root div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component structure isn't quite right. Create a constant named App with a setup function that returns a template containing a root div.

steps.title: Wrap app content with AuthProvider
steps.instruction: In the App component's template, wrap the existing content with the AuthProvider component.
steps.hint: Use the AuthProvider component as a wrapper element around your app's content in the template.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component's template should have the AuthProvider component wrapping the existing content.
successCriteria: AuthProvider component wraps the template content in the App component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wrapped the app content with the AuthProvider component, making the auth context available to all child components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the AuthProvider component properly wraps all the template content in the App component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AuthProvider component is not correctly wrapping the app content. Check that you've placed it as a parent element around the existing template content.

steps.title: Initialize and mount the Vue app
steps.instruction: Initialize the Vue app using createApp() with your App component, then mount it to a DOM element with id 'app'.
steps.hint: Call createApp() with the App component as argument, then chain .mount() with the selector string '#app'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue app will be initialized with the App component and mounted to the DOM, making the application visible in the browser.
successCriteria: createApp() is called with App as argument, and .mount('#app') is chained to mount the app to the DOM.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized and mounted the Vue app. The application is now ready to run with the Auth Context setup.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling createApp() with the App component and mounting it to '#app'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The app initialization or mounting is incorrect. Check that you're using createApp(App) and .mount('#app').
